answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with one-time vouchers backed by collateral. A newcomer posts a bond and gathers k vouchers from k different bonded peers; each voucher is burned on first use. The registry's prism view splits the graph into branches, so identities sharing a voucher collapse into one node. A mirror account copying another's credentials fails because those vouchers are spent. Periodic falcon audits demand a fresh signed reply, proving the key is live. Each fake agent costs a bond plus k vouchers, so attacking costs more than the rewards.
